Application Materials.content:
- Supporting documents usually include: **evidence of qualifications (certificates or transcripts)**; evidence of English language ability, if English is not your first language; **a research proposal** (check the department website for instructions as these vary); and any **additional requirements** set by the department (for example, some courses ask for specific information in a personal statement).
- You may need **two references**; referees will be contacted and asked to submit a reference directly via the referee portal, so applicants should make sure referees are aware in advance.
- If any certificates or transcripts have been issued in a language other than English, you should include **official, authenticated English translations**.
- The translation should be on official letter-headed paper, clearly state that it is an accurate translation of the original, and include: the translator or translation company's name and contact details; credentials or qualifications; the date of translation; and the translator's full name and signature, or the full name and signature of an authorised official from the translation company.
- The translation should be done by an official translator/translation service; translations by agents are not accepted unless the agency offers a recognised translation service and the translator can demonstrate appropriate credentials.

Application Deadlines.content:
- **Applications for 2026 entry** operate under a **staged admissions** process with selection deadlines throughout the year.
- **Stage 1:** Application received by **7th December 2025**; application update by **20th February 2026**.
- **Stage 2:** Application received by **1st March 2026**; application update by **1st May 2026**.
- **Stage 3:** Application received by **3rd May 2026**; application update by **19th June 2026**.
- **Stage 4:** Application received by **5th July 2026**; application update by **31st July 2026**.
- Applications received after the final selection deadline will be considered at the University's discretion if places are still available.
- **Year of entry: 2026**; fees are listed for entry in the academic year beginning **September 2026**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **High 2:1 honours degree (or overseas equivalent)**.
- For this pathway, applicants are expected to evidence an interest and/or experience in topics related to urban analysis. Examples include:
- working experience in urban-themed topics (e.g. data analyses for spatial phenomena, public policies or real estate market analysis);
- experience in working in spatial or GIS-based data analysis;
- evidence of training in urban-themed methods or topics (e.g. GIS).
- Applicants should demonstrate aptitude, knowledge and/or interest in three areas: **data analytics and/or statistics; computational subjects; and pathway specific requirements**. These can be demonstrated by course units taken at undergraduate level and high school level, or professional experience.
- The course welcomes applicants from a range of **STEM, business and humanities backgrounds**.
- For applicants from China (Mainland): taught master's applicants with a bachelor's degree from a recognised good-quality Chinese university, with a **minimum overall average grade of 80%** or a **minimum GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0)**, will generally be considered for admission to taught master's programmes; entry requirements differ between courses, so applicants should refer to the individual programme requirements for further guidance.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Applicants whose first language is not English should meet the following language requirements:
- **IELTS Academic: 7.0 overall** with **no component score below 6.5**.
- **TOEFL iBT: 100** with **no score below 22 in each section**. TOEFL code for Manchester is **0757**.
- **Pearson Test of English (PTE): 76 overall** with **no component score below 70**.
**Pre-Sessional English Courses**
- Applicants who do not meet these scores may be required to complete a pre-sessional English language course at the University of Manchester prior to the start of the course.
- **6 Week Pre-Sessional Course:** **IELTS 6.5 overall** with **6.0 in each sub-skill**.
- **10 Week Pre-sessional Course:** **IELTS 6.0 overall** with **6.0 in three sub-skills, and 5.5 in no more than one sub-skill**.
- If you have not yet completed your current academic study and are interested in studying a pre-sessional course, you must hold an **IELTS for UKVI (Academic)** test certificate to ensure that you are eligible for a separate visa for the English language course.
- Some English Language test results are only valid for **two years**. Your English Language test report must be valid on the **start date of the course**.
- Applicants from [majority English-speaking countries](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/admissions/language-requirements/) (or applicants who have studied for a full bachelor’s degree or higher from one of these countries) may be **exempt from submitting further evidence of English language proficiency**.

Program Overview.content:
- Duration: **1 year**. Degree: MSc. Study mode: Full-time, in person.
- This MSc Data Science (Urban Analytics) prepares students for data science careers with a focus on the data techniques and uses most relevant to urban analytics, including areas such as property, policy and town planning.
- The course is intended for graduates from a broad range of disciplines; applicants from STEM, business and humanities backgrounds are welcomed.
- Students develop skills in data analysis, project design, computational methods, and data stewardship. The course aims to train students to ask important research questions, evaluate the quality of available evidence, select appropriate methods, and use analytical skills to visualise, interpret and provide strategic advice and insight.
- The programme takes an interdisciplinary approach, covering varied aspects and applications of data science from Statistics, Demography, Social Networks, Data Science, Economics, Politics, Criminology, Health, Sociology, and other fields.
- Teaching is delivered by an interdisciplinary team through lectures, computer-based practicals, workshops, online courses and surgeries, meetings with industry partners, group work, and individual research.
- The master's degree comprises 180 credits. 120 credits are made up of a mix of mandatory and optional course units, and the remaining 60 credits are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of a **12,000-to-15,000-word dissertation** supported by weekly research methodology lectures.
- Graduates develop a skillset aimed at careers across policy, business, research and more; previous students have gone on to roles such as data scientists, civil servants, consultants, researchers, entrepreneurs, and roles within AI. The course is described as providing data skills for careers in banking and financial services, the Civil Service, the IT and tech sector, high performance sports analysis, large retail chains, the pharmaceutical industry, and urban planning. Students also have access to the University's [Careers Service](https://www.careers.manchester.ac.uk/) during the course and for two years after graduation.
- The course is eligible for the 1+3 studentship offered by the Economic and Social Sciences Research Council (ESRC) North West Social Sciences Doctoral Training Partnership (NWSSDTP), providing a fully funded route into postgraduate research and a pathway from master's-level study to a PhD. [Find out more on our 1+3 ESRC NWSSDTP webpage.](https://www.humanities.manchester.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-research/funding/list-of-awards/1-3-esrc-nwssdtp/#:~:text=Open%20to%20applicants%20from%20all,structured%20pathway%20into%20postgraduate%20research.)

Curriculum.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**.
- **Mode:** **Full-time: In person**.
- A master’s degree is formed of **180 credits**. **120** of these credits are made up by a mix of mandatory and optional course units, worth **15 credits each**. You will need to select **eight** of these course units, with **60 credits taken each semester**.
- The core units are: Machine Learning and Statistics (both semesters); Understanding Databases; Understanding Data and their Environment; Applications in Data Science.
- Optional course units range from statistical foundations to property valuation and digital planning.
- The remaining **60 credits** are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of a **12,000-to-15,000-word dissertation**. Your dissertation must be within the area of one of the course units you have chosen.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
- If your **School or Department Admissions Team agrees** to your request to defer, you may do so **without paying a deposit**.
- If you’ve already paid the deposit and then decide to defer, your payment will be **carried over** and used towards your tuition fees for the new entry year.
- If the **CAS deposit increases** for your new entry year, you’ll need to **pay the difference before your new CAS can be issued**.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Applicants who do not meet the English language scores for this programme **may be required to complete a pre-sessional English language course at the University of Manchester prior to the start of the course**. To be considered for a pre-sessional English language course for this programme, the following minimum IELTS (Academic) scores are required:
- **6 Week Pre-Sessional Course**: **IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each sub-skill**
- **10 Week Pre-sessional Course**: **IELTS 6.0 overall with 6.0 in three sub-skills, and 5.5 in no more than one sub-skill**
If you have not yet completed your current academic study and are interested in studying a pre-sessional course, you **must hold an IELTS for UKVI (Academic) test certificate** to ensure that you are eligible for a separate visa for the English language course.
